next_item_hypothesis: Demonstrated failure: an item SID that assigns a directed successor and its source to unrelated L1 regions can make the downstream next-item generator fail to retrieve the observed successor from a chronological history. In the train-only longest-prefix population, 314605 of 339519 directed transitions have no observed reverse event (fraction 0.9266197178950221), alongside mean next-item entropy 4.844072338042215 bits. These measurements establish asymmetric, branching transition behavior, not causal benefit or curvature. Hypothesis: a transition-supervised hyperbolic residual code assignment will place heterogeneous successor branches in a hierarchy around their source while preserving content reconstruction, improving L1 transition compatibility and leaving later levels to refine item identity. Stage2 creates one global SID per item and never ranks candidates.

math_definition.representation: For each item i, content encoder output h_i in R^d is mapped by the existing shared projection W,b to z_i=Wh_i+b in R^32. Three residual codebooks C_l in R^(256x32) produce q_{i,l}; initialize and optimize exactly as the frozen Stage2 baseline. Set r_{i,0}=z_i. For l=1,2,3 in order: (1) map the current residual with the curvature-dependent exponential map, (2) project the mapped vector to the common ball B_R, (3) assign k_{i,l}=argmin_{k in {1,...,256}} D_c^2(P_R(Exp_0^c(r_{i,l-1})), P_R(Exp_0^c(C_{l,k})), breaking ties by lowest k, (4) subtract the selected Euclidean code vector to obtain r_{i,l}=r_{i,l-1}-C_{l,k_{i,l}}. Each residual update is thus subtracted only after assignment and is mapped/projected before its next distance score. This yields the single stable, global SID (k_i1,k_i2,k_i3) for item i; no user, batch, history, or request enters assignment. The representation map and ball are identical in both arms.
math_definition.geometry_constants: Freeze c=1.0 for the hyperbolic arm, tau=0.1, epsilon=1e-5, R=1-epsilon, and clamp delta=1e-7. For every scored vector first apply P_R(x)=x when ||x||<=R and R*x/||x|| otherwise. The Poincare exponential map at the origin is Exp_0^c(v)=tanh(sqrt(c)||v||)*v/(sqrt(c)||v||), with value 0 at v=0. Evaluate arcosh(u) stably as log1p((u-1)+sqrt((u-1)*(u+1))) after setting u=max(1+delta, 1+2c||x-y||^2/((1-c||x||^2)(1-c||y||^2))). For the flat arm use the same code path's c->0 limit: Exp is the identity, every vector is still projected to the same B_R, and the radius formula (1-epsilon)/sqrt(c) is undefined at c=0 and is not applied; R remains the fixed shared projection radius. The scored squared distance has exact limit 4||x-y||^2. The distance itself tends to 2||x-y||. Both objective arms use the squared distance, never the unsquared distance.
math_definition.scored_distance: For projected x,y in B_R and c>0, D_c^2(x,y)=d_c(x,y)^2=(1/c)*arcosh(1 + 2c*||x-y||^2/((1-c*||x||^2)*(1-c*||y||^2)))^2. Its c->0 limit is 4*||x-y||^2; d_c(x,y) tends to 2*||x-y||. The flat arm scores the squared-distance limit, 4*||x-y||^2.
math_definition.transition_target_distribution: Let E={(a,b)} be the set of distinct ordered item transitions observed in the training split only and n_ab their training event counts. For each a with outgoing training edges let N(a)=sum_b n_ab and define T_ab=n_ab/N(a), indexed by b in O(a)={b:n_ab>0}; T has shape |E| in sparse edge form and each nonempty row sums to one. No validation/test/future event, prediction-time user context, or batch composition contributes. The frozen target is data-only and therefore has no target/parameter circularity.
loss_equations: For a training edge (a,b) in E, let X_i=P_R(Exp_0^c(z_i)) in the curved arm and X_i=P_R(z_i) in the flat limit. Let L_tr=-(1/|A|) sum_{a in A} sum_{b in O(a)} T_ab log[ exp(-D_c^2(X_a,X_b)/tau) / sum_{j in V_train} exp(-D_c^2(X_a,X_j)/tau) ], where A={a:O(a) nonempty}, V_train is the fixed Stage2 training-item set, and the denominator includes every item in V_train. Normalize first within each source row and then uniformly over A. Empty A is an invalid run (no replacement loss); nonfinite or zero denominator is NULL. Target T is computed once from training data and stop-gradient/data-only.

Let Q_i=sum_{l=1}^3 C_{l,k_{i,l}} be the stopped-assignment Euclidean reconstruction and let z_i be the 32-dimensional encoder output. L_rec=(1/|I_train|) sum_{i in I_train} ||z_i-stopgrad(Q_i)||_2^2, and L_commit=(1/|I_train|) sum_{i in I_train} ||stopgrad(z_i)-Q_i||_2^2. The empty item set is invalid; normalize uniformly over training items. These are unchanged baseline reconstruction/commitment terms in both arms.
L_total=L_rec+L_commit+L_tr, with no additional loss weights or schedule. L_tr uses only the stated squared distance and temperature; all sums and means are exactly those defined above.
math_definition.conditioning: No SID level conditions on earlier codes during assignment: each level's residual is conditioned only on the preceding residual formed by subtracting the previously assigned code vectors. No probability model over code prefixes is trained.
math_definition.protocol_freeze: Use the existing Stage2 content encoder, optimizer, learning rate/schedule, batch size, seeds, codebook initialization, data split, and complete 3000-epoch budget unchanged. No early stopping, sweep, extra recommender component, prefix Transformer, beam search, or candidate ranking. The geometry comparison is one implementation parameterized by c, with identical architecture, parameter count, initialization, optimizer, schedule, seeds, projection region, and training budget; only the distance formula varies.

hyperbolic_necessity: The measured transition graph has many observed one-way edges and high next-item entropy; a flat geometry must spend representational capacity on heterogeneous branching with uniform Euclidean distances, whereas negative curvature can allocate more volume to outward branching while retaining short shared-prefix distances near a hierarchy's root. This is a mechanism-level rationale for testing curvature, not proof that the data are hierarchical or that hyperbolic geometry must win. The transition signal is used in both arms, so any difference isolates geometry rather than graph supervision.
euclidean_control: Same implementation, architecture, parameters, initialization, transition targets, losses, training-only inputs, common fixed projection ball, optimizer, schedule, seeds, and budget. Set c=0 and evaluate the exact limits of the same map and squared-distance code path; no separately designed Euclidean arm.
effect_site: Stage2 code assignment, codebook geometry, and the transition/reconstruction objective. Expected movement: valid L1 positive hit rate upward; valid Hard-L1 ER upward; level2_distinct_prefixes upward; L3 collision downward; L3 refinement gain upward; conditional G3 upward. These are diagnostics, not claims of demonstrated effects.
real_trigger_measurement: The frozen train-only transition manifest's sparse-reversal failure: no_observed_reverse_events=314605 of 339519 transitions (0.9266197178950221), with mean_next_item_entropy_bits=4.844072338042215. This motivates an experiment only; the manifest interpretation limit applies.
training_only_inputs: Item content embeddings and item transitions from the training split only. The transition counts/targets are static training-derived tensors. Validation is used only for the frozen diagnostics and test behavior only for the registered Stage3 comparison; neither enters fitting, assignment, target construction, or model selection. No future events, validation/test behavior, prediction-time user context, or batch composition.

stage2_diagnostics.name: valid L1 positive hit rate
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: paired frozen seeds; compute each seed on the exact 52855 frozen validation pairs (one positive and ten negatives per anchor, seed 42, history[-1] to target); aggregate by arithmetic mean of paired seed differences

stage2_diagnostics.name: valid Hard-L1 ER
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: paired frozen seeds; ER=10*positive_hits/negative_hits with negatives counted over the same ten negatives; aggregate arithmetic mean of paired differences

stage2_diagnostics.name: level2_distinct_prefixes
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: paired frozen seeds; count unique (k1,k2) over all items per seed; aggregate arithmetic mean of paired differences

stage2_diagnostics.name: L3 collision
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: paired frozen seeds; per-seed share of items whose (k1,k2,k3) is shared with another item; aggregate arithmetic mean of paired differences

stage2_diagnostics.name: L3 refinement gain
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: paired frozen seeds; per-seed mean over items of log2(|bucket(k1,k2)|/|bucket(k1,k2,k3)|); aggregate arithmetic mean of paired differences

stage2_diagnostics.name: conditional G3
stage2_diagnostics.seed_rule: paired frozen seeds; use the frozen validation pairs and train-transition history term mixed into the Laplace-smoothed (alpha=1 over 256 codes) prefix prior; aggregate arithmetic mean of paired differences

stage3_behavioral_test.seed_rule: paired identical frozen Stage3 seeds and all frozen Stage3 settings; compare test_R@10 once per seed and aggregate arithmetic mean of paired differences; no test-based selection or tuning

classification.falsified_if: any registered stage2_diagnostics minimum_effect is not met in its registered direction OR stage3_behavioral_test minimum_effect is not met in its registered direction, with no NULL seed in the comparison
classification.passed_if: every registered stage2_diagnostics minimum_effect and stage3_behavioral_test minimum_effect is met in its registered direction, with no NULL seed in any comparison
classification.mixed_if: at least one registered effect meets its minimum_effect in its registered direction and at least one other registered effect does not, with no NULL seed in any comparison

null_outcome_rule: If a seed-wise or aggregated change is undefined or non-finite (including zero denominator, missing evaluation, or empty stratum), classify that comparison NULL. Any comparison containing any NULL seed is inconclusive, neither passed nor falsified; do not impute or replace the value.
